{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{refimprove|date=February 2024}} {{Infobox NCAA team season | sport = basketball | year = 2015–16 | team = Maryland Terrapins | image = Maryland terrapins logo.png | image_size = 200px | image_alt = | conference = Big Ten Conference | short_conf = Big Ten | CoachRank = 13 | APRank = 18 | record = 27–9 | conf_record = 12–6 | head_coach = [[Mark Turgeon]] | hc_year = 5th | asst_coach1 = Dustin Clark | ac1_year = | asst_coach2 = Bino Ranson | ac2_year = | asst_coach3 = [[Cliff Warren]] | ac3_year = | arena = [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] | champion = [[Cancún Challenge|Cancún Challenge (Riviera)]] champions | tourney = [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2015–16 Big Ten men's basketball standings}} The '''2015–16 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by fifth year head coach [[Mark Turgeon]] and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]]. This was their second year as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season with a record of 27–9, 12–6 in [[2015-16 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a four-way tie for third place in conference. They defeated [[2015–16 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2015–16 South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball team|South Dakota State]] and [[2015–16 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors basketball team|Hawaii]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. In the Sweet Sixteen, they lost to [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]].{{cite news|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2016/03/25/ellis-selden-lead-kansas-past-maryland/82228570/|title=Ellis, Selden lead Kansas past Maryland|first=Jason|last=Frakes|work=[[Courier Journal]]|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2024}} ==Previous season== The [[2014-15 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]] with a record of 28–7, 14–4 in [[2014–15 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in second place in conference. They advanced to the semifinals of the [[2015 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] where they lost to [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2014–15 Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball team|Valparaiso]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2014–15 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]]. ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
